questions.question: Which of the following is incorrect about human eye ?

options.text: The iris controls the amount of light entering into eye
Cone cells are sensitive to bright light
At blind spot in eye, there is no vision

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is__** Rod cells sense colour**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• **The iris controls the amount of light entering into the eye: **This **statement is correct.** The iris is the colored part of the eye and consists of muscles that can contract or expand. By adjusting the size of the pupil (the black circular opening in the center of the iris), the iris controls the amount of light that enters the eye. In bright light, the iris contracts, making the pupil smaller to reduce the amount of light entering the eye. In dim light, the iris expands, making the pupil larger to allow more light into the eye.
 
• **Cone cells are sensitive to bright light:** This **statement is correct. **Cone cells are one of the two types of photoreceptor cells in the retina of the eye. **They are responsible for color vision and are most sensitive to bright light conditions.** Cone cells are concentrated in the fovea, the central part of the retina, which is responsible for high-resolution vision and color perception.
 
• **Rod cells sense color: **This** statement is incorrect. **Rod cells are the other type of photoreceptor cells in the retina. They are responsible for vision in dim light or low-light conditions, such as night vision. While** rod cells do not provide color vision, they are highly sensitive to light and allow us to see in low-light environments.**
 
• **At the blind spot in the eye, there is no vision: **This **statement is correct. **The blind spot in the eye, also known as **the optic disc, **is the area on the retina where** the optic nerve exits the eye. **This area lacks photoreceptor cells (both rods and cones), so there are no visual receptors to detect light. As a result, light that falls on the** blind spot cannot be detected,** and there is no vision in that specific part of the visual field. However, our brain compensates for this blind spot, and we usually do not notice it in our day-to-day activities.

questions.question: The curvature of the eye lens can be changed by
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ciliary muscles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The ability to alter the curvature of the eye's lens, a feature known as accommodation, is controlled by the ciliary muscles that are part of the eye's structure.**
 
• Ciliary muscles in the eye help change the shape of the eye's lens to allow our vision to focus on objects at various distances. 
 
• **When** **the muscles are relaxed, the curvature decreases making the lens thin and the focal length increases.**
 
• **Similarly when the ciliary muscles contract the curvature of the eye lens increases making them thicker, this decreases the focal length of the eye**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The retina, pupil, and iris are critical parts of the eye, each featuring unique functions, but they do not influence the curvature of the lens.
 
• **The retina is a layer at the back of the eyeball that contains cells sensitive to light. These cells trigger nerve impulses that pass via the optic nerve to the brain, where a visual image is formed.**
 
• The pupil is the opening in the iris that allows light to enter the retina. It changes size according to light conditions, but it doesn't affect the curvature of the lens.
 
• The iris is the colored portion of the eye that controls the amount of light that reaches the retina through the pupil. It doesn't change the lens's curvature.

questions.question: On which of the following principle does the human eye work?
questions.solution:
The correct option is**__ Refraction of light__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The eye of a human being is like a camera**
 
• So basically, light rays that are deflected from or by distant objects land on the retina after they pass through various mediums like the cornea, crystalline lens, aqueous humor, the lens, and vitreous humor.
 
• The concept here though is that as the light rays move through the various mediums, they experience refraction of light.
 
• The bending of light rays in the denser medium is known as Refraction.
 
• When a light ray travels from a lighter to a denser medium, the light ray bends towards the normal.
 
• When a light ray travels from a denser to a lighter medium the light ray bends away from the normal.

questions.question: In the normal eye, the distance of the retina from the eye lens is 2.5 cm. The power of the eye lens when it is focussed at its near point 25 cm from the eye is :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**44D**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **distance between the eye lens and the retina is the image distance (v), which is 2.5 cm.**
 
• The near point is the closest distance at which the eye can focus,** which is the object distance (u), and is given as 25 cm.**
 
• **Lens Formula:** The lens formula relates the object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) of a lens:
 
• 1/f = 1/v - 1/u
 
• **Applying the Formula:** In our case:
 
 
• 1/f = 1/2.5 - 1/(-25)
 
• 1/f = 1/2.5 + 1/25
 
• 1/f = (10 + 1) / 25
 
• 1/f = 11/25
 
• f = 25/11 cm
 
• v = 2.5 cm
 
• u = -25 cm (negative sign because the object is on the left side of the lens)
 
 
 
• **Power of the Lens:** The power (P) of a lens in diopters (D) is the reciprocal of its focal length in meters:
 
 
• P = 1/f (where f is in meters)
 
• First, convert the focal length to meters:
 
• f = (25/11) / 100 = 0.25/11 m
 
• Now, calculate the power:
 
• P = 1/(0.25/11) = 11/0.25 = 44 D

questions.question: The focal length of human eye lens is (with relaxed eye)-
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 2.5 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Focal Length**: The focal length of the lens is the distance between the lens and the image sensor when the subject is in focus.
 
• The human eye encompasses a **biconvex lens**.
 
• The lens within the eye refracts the light and focuses it on the retina. 
 
• The shape of the lens changes to **regulate the focal length of the eye**, thus allowing the eye to focus clearly on objects at varying distances.
 
• The ability of the lens to adjust from far to near focus is called **accommodation.**
 
• The eye focuses on an object by bending all of the light rays from a single point on the observed object toward a single point on the retina.
 
• In the eyeball, light rays passing through the cornea are bent by its curvature toward the pupil.
 
• The lens flexes to change its curvature and finish the focusing process.
 
• When an object is located at infinity, **the focal length, or the distance from the cornea to the retina, of a normal relaxed eye is** about **2.5 cm**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Myopia: **

 
• **Myopia** is also referred to** as near-sightedness.**
 
• It** **is an eye disorder where light focuses in front of, instead of on, the retina. As a result of which, **distant objects appear blurry while close objects appear normal.**

**Hypermetropia:**

 
• Hypermetropia is also known as **far-sightedness.**
 
• **It** is the condition of the eyes where the image of a nearby object is formed behind the retina.
 
• Here, the light is focused behind the retina instead of focusing on the retina.
 
• The person suffering from hypermetropia has **difficulty seeing nearby objects clearly but can see distant objects clearly**.

**Presbyopia:**

 
• **Presbyopia is the gradual loss of your eye's ability to focus on nearby objects**. 
 
• Presbyopia usually starts in the early to mid-40s and continues to worsen until around age 65.

questions.question: The defect of vision in human beings in which the power of accommodation of the eye decreases with aging and the near point gradually recedes away is known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Presbyopia**__.

__
 
• The defect of vision in human beings in which the power of accommodation of the eye decreases with aging and the near point gradually recedes away is known as **Presbyopia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Presbyopia:

 
 
• ​The power of accommodation of the eye usually decreases with aging.
 
• For most people, the near point gradually recedes away.
 
• They find it difficult to see nearby objects comfortably and distinctly without corrective eyeglasses.
 
• This defect is called Presbyopia. It arises due to the gradual weakening of the ciliary muscles and diminishing flexibility of the eye lens.
 
• Sometimes, a person may suffer from both myopia and hypermetropia.
 
• Such people often require bifocal lenses.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hypermetropia:

 
 
• Long-sightedness, also known as hypermetropia or hyperopia is a common vision disorder.
 
• It results from the overall power of the eye not being strong enough, or the length of the eye being too short.
 
• A surgical correction is a treatment option for hypermetropia, including laser eye surgery and clear lens exchange.
 
• This defect can be corrected by using a convex lens of appropriate power.
 
 
 
• Myopia:
 
 
• ​Nearsightedness (myopia) is a common vision condition in which you can see objects near to you clearly, but objects farther away are blurry.
 
• It occurs when the shape of your eye causes light rays to bend (refract) incorrectly, focusing images in front of your retina instead of on your retina.
 
 
 
• Cataract:
 
 
• ​A cataract is a clouding of the normally clear lens of your eye.
 
• For people who have cataracts, seeing through cloudy lenses is a bit like looking through a frosty or fogged-up window.
 
• The main symptom is blurry vision.

questions.question: If a person can see far objects distinctly but cannot see nearby objects clearly, then this eye defect can be corrected by using ______.

options.text: a concave lens of suitable power
a convex lens of suitable power

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a convex lens of suitable power**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The condition where a person can see distant objects clearly but has difficulty seeing nearby objects is called **hypermetropia** or farsightedness.
 
• Hypermetropia occurs when the eyeball is too short or the lens is not curved enough, causing light to focus behind the retina.
 
• This condition can be corrected by using a **convex lens** of suitable power.
 
• A convex lens converges light rays before they enter the eye, thus allowing the light to focus directly on the retina.
 
• Using a convex lens helps in adjusting the focal length so that nearby objects can be seen clearly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Myopia**

 
 
• Myopia, or nearsightedness, is a condition where a person can see nearby objects clearly but has difficulty seeing distant objects.
 
• It is usually corrected using concave lenses, which diverge light rays before they enter the eye.
 
 
 
• **Astigmatism**
 
 
• Astigmatism is a common vision condition caused by an irregularly shaped cornea or lens.
 
• It can cause blurred or distorted vision at all distances and is usually corrected with cylindrical lenses.
 
 
 
• **Presbyopia**
 
 
• Presbyopia is an age-related condition where the eye's lens loses its flexibility, making it difficult to focus on close objects.
 
• This condition can be corrected using bifocal or progressive lenses that have different sections for distance and near vision.

questions.question: The outermost fibrous coating of the eye is called-
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sclera**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The outermost fibrous coating of the eye is called the **Sclera**.
 
• The sclera is a tough, white protective layer that provides structure and protection to the eye.
 
• It is continuous with the cornea at the front of the eye and extends around the entire eyeball.
 
• The sclera is commonly referred to as the "white of the eye" and serves as an attachment site for the eye muscles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **ciliary body** is part of the eye's middle layer and is involved in the production of aqueous humor and the accommodation of the lens.
 
• The **iris** is the colored part of the eye that controls the size of the pupil and the amount of light that enters the eye.
 
• The **choroid** is a vascular layer of the eye containing connective tissue and lying between the retina and the sclera.
 
• The **cornea** is the transparent front part of the eye that covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber and provides most of the eye's optical power.

questions.question: Which part of the eye regulates and control the amount of light entering the human eye?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Iris__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The iris is a thin, circular structure in the eye responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil.
 
• It regulates the amount of light entering the eye by adjusting the pupil size, which is essential for optimal vision.
 
• The iris contains muscles that contract and expand to adjust the pupil size in response to varying light conditions.
 
• The color of the iris is what gives the eye its color, varying from blue, green, brown, etc.
 
• The process by which the iris adjusts the pupil size is known as the pupillary light reflex.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Retina**

 
 
• The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye that converts light into electrical signals.
 
• It contains photoreceptor cells called rods and cones that detect light intensity and color.
 
• The retina plays a crucial role in forming visual images and transmitting them to the brain via the optic nerve.
 
 
 
• **Cornea**
 
 
• The cornea is the transparent, dome-shaped front layer of the eye that covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber.
 
• It plays a key role in focusing light onto the retina, contributing to the eye's overall refractive power.
 
• The cornea is avascular, meaning it has no blood vessels, and receives nutrients from tears and aqueous humor.
 
 
 
• **Pupil**
 
 
• The pupil is the black circular opening in the center of the iris that allows light to enter the eye.
 
• Its size is regulated by the iris muscles, contracting in bright light and dilating in low light to control light intake.
 
• The pupil's adjustment is an essential part of the eye's response to different lighting conditions.

questions.question:
Neha’s Mother discovers that she is facing difficulty in reading the newspaper. Her doctor prescribed spectacles for her. Which of the following statements is/are true:

i. She suffers from hypermetropia where the near point is farther than the newspaper.

ii. A convex lens with a suitable power can help correct her vision.

iii. Her eye is defective and is forming image/jpgs behind the retina.

iv. A concave lens or a convex lens may be used to correct her vision
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Neha's mother is suffering from **hypermetropia**, a condition where the near point of her eye is farther than normal, making it difficult to focus on nearby objects like a newspaper.
 
• In hypermetropia, the **image is formed behind the retina**, leading to difficulty in near vision.
 
• A **convex lens** is prescribed to correct hypermetropia as it helps converge light rays onto the retina.
 
• Hypermetropia is primarily caused by either a **shortened eyeball** or reduced curvature of the lens, making it less effective at focusing light.
 
• The statements i, ii, and iii are correct, as they describe the condition and the corrective measure accurately.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hypermetropia (Farsightedness):**

 
 
• It is a refractive defect of vision where distant objects are seen clearly but nearby objects appear blurred.
 
• It can be corrected using a convex lens to focus light rays onto the retina.
 
• Common causes include genetic factors, aging, or structural abnormalities of the eye.
 
 
 
• **Convex Lens:**
 
 
• A convex lens is thicker in the middle and converges light rays.
 
• It is used to treat hypermetropia by adjusting the focal point onto the retina.
 
 
 
• **Retina and Image Formation:**
 
 
• The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye where images are formed.
 
• In hypermetropia, images are formed behind the retina due to improper focusing.
 
 
 
• **Other Common Vision Defects:**
 
 
• Myopia (nearsightedness): Corrected with concave lenses.
 
• Presbyopia: Age-related loss of near vision, often requiring bifocal or progressive lenses.

The correct answer is __**Blind spot**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The blind spot in the human eye is the area on the retina where the **optic nerve exits the eye**, also known as the optic disc.
 
• This region lacks photoreceptor cells (rods and cones), making it **insensitive to light**.
 
• The blind spot is located slightly **nasal to the fovea in the visual field of each eye**.
 
• Despite the presence of a blind spot, the brain compensates for it by using information from the other eye or by filling in the missing details, making it **unnoticeable under normal circumstances**.
 
• The phenomenon of the blind spot was first discovered by the French scientist **Edme Mariotte** in the 17th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fovea**

 
 
• The fovea is a small depression in the retina that contains a high concentration of cones.
 
• It is responsible for **sharp central vision**, enabling activities like reading and driving.
 
 
 
• **Photoreceptor Cells**
 
 
• There are two types of photoreceptor cells in the retina: **rods** and **cones**.
 
• Rods are sensitive to low light and help in night vision, while cones are responsible for color vision and work better in bright light.
 
 
 
• **Optic Nerve**
 
 
• The optic nerve transmits visual information from the retina to the brain.
 
• It is composed of over a million nerve fibers and plays a crucial role in the visual system.
 
 
 
• **Visual Field**
 
 
• The visual field is the total area visible to an eye when it is focused on a central point.
 
• Each eye has its own blind spot, and their positioning prevents overlap in binocular vision.

questions.question: What is the horizontal field view of one eye in human beings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**150°**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The human eye** is like **a camera**. Its lens system forms an image on a light-sensitive screen called the **retina**.
 
• The **eyeball** is approximately spherical in shape with a **diameter of about 2.3 cm**.
 
• The **eye lens** forms an** inverted real image** of the object on the **retina**.
 
• The** light-sensitive cells** get activated upon** illumination and generate electrical signals**. These signals are sent to the brain via the optic nerves. The brain interprets these signals, and finally, processes the information so that we perceive objects as they are. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When** the light** is very **bright**, the** iris** contracts the** pupil** to allow** less light to enter**
 
• However, in **dim light**, the** iris expands **the pupil to **allow more light to enter**
 
• Thus, the** pupil opens** completely through the relaxation of the iris.
 
• **A human being has a horizontal field of view of about 150° with one eye **and about 180° with two eyes. **Hence option 1 is correct. **
